PullRequest.Title: agentHost: drain debounced summary writes before saved-chat continuation archives (un-skip flaky test)
PullRequest.Body:

Un-skips `AgentHostSavedChatContinuation` › `records a busy source completion and retries archive when its turn has finished`, skipped as flaky in #341725 (c2d44a14b50), and fixes the race it exposed in `AgentService.completeSavedChatContinuation`.

## Original failures

It failed 8 times as a confirmed flake (it passed on retry) between Oct 14 and 15, every time with `idle: { archived: false }` where `true` was expected (`AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly deep-equal`).

| Job | Retry that passed | Branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Windows / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38626906350/job/116069004827) | attempt 2 | `agents/fix-session-comparison-list-rendering` |
| [Windows / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38627066400/job/116069138128) | attempt 2 | `hawkticehurst/migration-tooltip-labels` |
| [Windows / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38627142766/job/116069736595) | attempt 3 | `connor4312/9126` |
| [Windows / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38634234144/job/116093190881) | attempt 2 | `sandy081/agents/move-wordwrap-to-overflow-menu` |
| [Windows / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38652861821/job/116156096965) | attempt 2 | `bv/automation-run-feedback-overnight` |
| [Windows / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38657193147/job/116169644853) | attempt 3 | `roblou/agents/fix-vscode-issue-338415` |
| [Windows / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38686957653/job/116263904513) | attempt 2 | `fix/customizations-marketplace-sign-in` |
| [macOS / Electron-Unit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38693423380/job/116284369126) | attempt 2 | `lszomoru/agents/fix-branch-picker-initialization-bug` |

The test came in with f9eda2440cb (#340702) and flaked from the start. #341721 (811e884bc22), which landed right after the skip, only changed the fixture's worktree hooks and is not involved: `worktreeCalls` is `[]` in every failure.

## Root cause

`ChatTurnStarted` and `ChatTurnComplete` mark the session summary dirty. `SessionSummaryNotifier` publishes the change after a real **100ms `RunOnceScheduler` debounce**. `AgentService` then calls `_queueCatalogSync`, which starts a background `_persistListVisibleSessionStateNow` that writes the session's list-visible state into `session.db`, including the pre-archive `isArchived = ''`.

`completeSavedChatContinuation` already waits for `_whenBackgroundCatalogStateWritesIdle`. That only covers writes that are already queued, not one still in the debounce window. So the write can start after the continuation has checked for background writes and land on top of the archive. A temporary probe on the session database's metadata writers recorded this order in a failing iteration:

```
setMetadataValuesAndCatalogSyncSnapshot ''     ← _persistListVisibleSessionStateNow (turn start)
setMetadataValuesAndCatalogSyncSnapshot 'true' ← _archiveSavedChatContinuation
setMetadataValuesAndCatalogSyncSnapshot ''     ← _persistListVisibleSessionStateNow (turn complete, stale)
applyMetadataChanges 'true'                    ← session state store (SessionIsArchivedChanged)
```

Reading between the third and fourth write gives the CI failure (`idle.archived === false`). When the first write lands before the test reads `before`, you get the other variant seen while stress-testing (`before === ''` where `undefined` was expected). Outside tests, the session is briefly un-archived on disk until the next write.

## Fix

- `AgentHostStateManager.flushPendingSessionSummary(session)` publishes a session's pending summary change immediately, the same way `removeSession` and `prepareSessionSummariesForListing` already do.
- `completeSavedChatContinuation` calls it before `_whenBackgroundCatalogStateWritesIdle`, so the catalog write for a just-started or just-finished turn is queued and drained *before* the archive runs.
- The test is un-skipped. Its `before` check previously asserted `undefined`, which only held when the debounced write had not landed yet, so it was asserting on the race. It now asserts what it means: the busy completion did not archive (`isArchived !== 'true'`).

## Stress results

Same test, looped 300 times per Electron process:

| Where | Load | Before fix | After fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (local) | none | **97 / 900 failed** (3, 37 and 57 per run) | **0 / 300** |
| macOS (local) | one busy loop per core | **26 / 900 failed** | **0 / 900** |
| Windows / Electron-Unit CI (diagnostic draft #342352) | none | 0 / 900 ([job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39080755489/job/117537026003)) | – |
| Windows / Electron-Unit CI (diagnostic draft #342352) | 8 busy loops (one per core) | **8 / 900 failed** ([job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39081590471/job/117539612654)) | **0 / 900** ([job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39082263761/job/117541478991)) |

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostSavedChatContinuation.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostSavedChatService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostStateManager.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionArtifactRemoval.test.ts`: passed, 1716 passing, 0 failing.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Complete an idle saved-chat continuation while a live source has a debounced turn-summary change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The renderer has already created/loaded and opened the Copilot destination before awaiting completeSavedChatContinuation. The RPC completion path waits for source residency release, now synchronously emits the pending summary, waits for its catalog synchronization, waits for source/destination peer-chat stores, then performs existing saved-history/database validation and archive persistence. The moved catalog write is on the RPC's completion-state path but not on the destination-opening path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-RPC vscode/completeSavedChatContinuation request from renderer to agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request and handler were used before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited after the destination is opened; gates marking the in-memory destination record completed

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist list-visible session state through session database and central catalog synchronization
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existing pending write is forced for the source session before archival; the per-session background writer coalesces concurrent changes into a trailing write
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same dirty summary scheduled this write after the 100 ms debounce, but completion could pass _whenBackgroundCatalogStateWritesIdle before it was queued, leaving it off the awaited path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff moves an already-debounced write onto the continuation RPC completion path so archival cannot be overwritten by its stale pre-archive snapshot

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read saved backing/history and session metadata, write continuation receipt, and synchronize archive metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing bounded sequence for one source and destination; aggregate archive inspection scales with the source's public chats
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical saved-chat validation, receipt, and archive operations occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by completion and dominates the existing continuation/archive workflow

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source session per request. The newly awaited synchronization serializes the source summary/catalog, whose work scales with that session's chat collection; it is not multiplied across all sessions. Saved-history and public-chat scans are pre-existing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Continuation attempts are serialized by source key in _savedChatContinuations. Catalog writes are serialized and trailing-coalesced per source in _backgroundCatalogStateWrites; peer-chat operations are awaited for only source and destination. Different sessions can proceed independently, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SessionSummaryNotifier's dirty set and 100 ms scheduler are the relevant coalescing state. The diff consumes only an existing dirty entry; clean sessions do no new work. There is no new cache, key retention, negative-cache state, or changed cold/warm lookup behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in call path, cardinality, ordering, and boundary placement from the changed line, synchronous notifier listener, per-session writer, renderer caller, and persistence implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local database synchronization duration varies by storage and catalog size, but this is one already-scheduled write moved earlier rather than a new recurring operation, and destination presentation has already completed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The changed placement is required to order an already-pending write before archive, is bounded to one source session, and does not add total write cardinality on this scenario.

Scenarios.Scenario: Attempt continuation while the live source is busy, then retry after its turn completes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each per-source attempt is serialized. The busy attempt now flushes and awaits the turn-start summary write before existing continuation validation returns archived:false; after turn completion, the retry flushes and awaits the turn-complete summary before existing archive work. Destination UI presentation precedes the initial completion RPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Catalog synchronization triggered by flushing the dirty turn-start or turn-complete summary
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one forced source-session write per attempt when dirty; repeated same-source attempts serialize, and writes coalesce per session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The turn summary still caused the same asynchronous catalog write after the debounce, but a completion attempt could return before it was queued.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the completion attempt instead of occurring after the debounce

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing saved-history reads, destination catalog checks, continuation receipt update, and archive metadata synchronization on the successful retry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded operation sequence per attempt; successful aggregate decisions scale with public chats
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same attempt and retry operations existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited completion work; the busy attempt avoids archive persistence but still records/validates the continuation

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of user continuation attempts for one source and that source's public chats. The changed work does not fan out per turn or across sessions; effective cardinality is one pending summary synchronization per dirty attempt.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-source attempts queue behind _savedChatContinuations, and source catalog writes serialize/coalesce. No new burst is introduced; cross-session independence is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Turn-start and turn-complete updates share the notifier dirty set but are separated by an awaited attempt in this scenario. A clean retry makes flushPendingSessionSummary a no-op. No retained keys or miss retries are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the busy path awaits the moved write and remains per-session serialized; lower certainty only concerns local write duration and how often users continue a still-running saved source.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A busy attempt can now await a local catalog write that previously completed in the background, but the write was already guaranteed by the turn-summary debounce, this workflow is one-shot and post-presentation, and evidence does not establish user-visible latency or increased total I/O.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff changes timing but not total boundary-call cardinality, and the bounded post-presentation delay is insufficient to establish an actionable performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Complete a cold surfaced or clean live saved-chat continuation with no pending summary
Scenarios.CriticalPath: flushPendingSessionSummary checks the notifier dirty set and returns synchronously. Existing peer-store waits, saved-chat reads, receipt persistence, and archive synchronization remain the only expensive work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing saved-chat history/metadata reads and archive writes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source/destination completion sequence, with pre-existing public-chat-dependent validation

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source continuation; existing work scales with saved history and public chats. The added dirty-set lookup is constant time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-source completion serialization and existing database coordination are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold surfaced sessions have no live summary dirty entry, and clean live sessions have no pending entry, so the new method performs no persistence or serialization. No cache lifecycle changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed mechanism; it is a constant-time Set lookup.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete three-file diff and traced the pending-summary flush through synchronous listeners, per-session catalog write coalescing, continuation serialization, saved-chat validation, archive persistence, protocol IPC, and renderer presentation. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found, and the PR fixes a correctness race rather than a documented performance regression.
